description:
## Goal
Range and Map users of the shared Enum.reduce* bridge must reach a single settled transport plan, not abort at the shape-anchor meet (reduce/2) or at native callable materialization (to_list Range+Map). The semantic drive already converges; the live defect is in TRANSPORT shape derivation, not the semantic return join.

## Root cause (ground truth, HEAD 8a91e9c90, reduce/2 worked example)
For `Enum.reduce(1..7//2, fn (x, acc) -> x * acc end)`:
- Enum.reduce/2 (fn 67) builds inner lambda L = `fn (entry, state) -> reduce_first_step(entry, state, reducer) end` (FunctionId 174), capturing the user reducer. The closure record physically holds ONE capture slot (the boxed reducer callable).
- reduce_first_step/3 (fn 114) has two clauses keyed on `state`: `reduce_first_step(entry, :first, _reducer)` IGNORES the reducer; `reduce_first_step(entry, {:acc, acc}, reducer)` CALLS it. So L specializes into two activations by state type: A (state = :first sentinel, Ty50) and B (state = {:acc,_} tuple, Ty116).
- The reducer-capture input (sem_index 0) of activation A is anchored by TWO transport passes that DISAGREE:
  - seed-callable-flow-capture-inputs (transport.rs:1710) derives the capture shape from the consuming activation's USE-demand via shape_for_local_value. On the :first path nothing reads the reducer, so the backward demand bottoms to Ignore -> ShapeId Nothing.
  - seed_callable_resolution_capture_inputs (transport.rs:1738) derives it from the closure's canonical interned descr.capture_shapes -> ShapeId Callable.
  - Nothing vs Callable for the SAME capture slot of the SAME closure value -> ShapeConstraintGraph component_shapes agree-or-panic meet (transport.rs:338) fires (ShapeId(11) != ShapeId(14)).
- to_list Range+Map (bfh.4) fails one layer down with 'native callable materialization matched multiple native boundaries' for the same bridge lambda; provisionally the same closure-layout fragmentation surfacing at native lowering. MUST be re-confirmed independently, not assumed.

A closure's capture layout is fixed at CONSTRUCTION; an activation that does not call a capture still carries it in the closure record. Collapsing a physically-present capture to Nothing because one specialized activation does not read it fragments a layout-identical closure -- the [[feedback_shapeid_is_pure_layout]] principle: transport ShapeId is physical layout, not use/contract.

## Required work
- Capture-input transport shapes must derive from the capture VALUE's construction-site physical layout (the closure record), NOT from a consuming activation's backward use-demand. The two seed passes (flow-demand at transport.rs:1710 and canonical descr at 1738) must agree by construction: one canonical source of capture-input shape, so a present-but-unused capture never anchors Nothing.
- Remove the now-redundant/conflicting anchoring path rather than reconciling two sources (remove what is no longer necessary).
- Confirm the to_list Range+Map native-boundary-multiplicity failure resolves from the same fix; if it has a distinct root, file it as its own ticket (do not fold silently).
- Remove the STALE defer.* flags from fz_f98_range_reduce_scalar (all three paths already pass on HEAD).
- Regression: fz_f98_range_reduce2 and fz_f98_range_map_converges reach transport/native within budget; reduce_scalar stays green; add a transport-level signal that a present-but-unused capture anchors the closure's canonical capture shape (not Nothing).

## Checks
- fz_f98_range_reduce2: shape-anchor meet no longer panics; settles through transport.
- fz_f98_range_map_converges: native callable materialization resolves one boundary per published transport boundary.
- fz_f98_range_reduce_scalar: remains green with defers removed.
- No new shape-anchor disagreements across the lib + matrix suites.

## NOT the problem (superseded)
The earlier framing (non-monotone return-ascent storm; make surface/return joins monotone) does NOT reproduce on HEAD -- f98.1/f98.2 already settled convergence; define_return already treats None as a no-op bottom on the join path. No storm exists. The fix is closure capture-layout identity in transport, not the semantic return join.

comments.text: INVESTIGATION CHECKPOINT (not yet implemented). Ground truth confirmed: f98.2's addressed-frame surface match is already correct -- runtime_demand.rs:519-522 compares own_surface (past captures) to surface.inputs and skips on mismatch, NOT a raw-slot compare. So f98.3's locus is the RETURN-EVIDENCE join, not the surface match. Per f98's pinned telemetry (~52941 activation_analysis re-derivations paired 1:1 with return_type; #1 oscillator Enum.reduce fn69; churning Map-reduce callsite with return_ty: None on Ty(19) -- same fn/type as fz-bfh.3's absent value), the storm is a NON-MONOTONE RETURN ASCENT: the shared bridge executable's return type drops back to None rather than widening monotonically once concrete evidence arrives ([[unknown-is-not-none]] / convergence-by-construction). FIX SHAPE (Output Contract Loop, fresh budget): (1) reproduce the range+map storm with the fz-bfh.7 JobBudgetGuard to name the oscillating kind loud; (2) trace to the exact site where the bridge return_ty is RE-GROUND to None instead of joined; (3) make the join widen-only -- absent stays None, proven-empty stays none(), concrete ascends by union only -- and DELETE the re-grounding (the 'remove what's no longer necessary'); (4) regression: range+map reduce/to_list compiles within the normal drive budget with bounded activation_analysis/return_type churn (guard-observed), ReturnType widening telemetry NOT the escape hatch. Did NOT implement at this session's context depth to avoid the sprawl class we just cleaned (see fz-bfh.5.5 history).

CORRECTED DIAGNOSIS (ran the three deferred fixtures with defers stripped on HEAD 8a91e9c90 — ground truth, not the stale pinned telemetry the prior checkpoint relied on):

NO STORM EXISTS. The semantic drive converges. The prior 'non-monotone return-ascent storm' hypothesis does NOT reproduce: a range+map reduce/3 probe reaches semantic closure AND transport in <4k jobs, and define_return already treats None as a no-op bottom on the join path. The ~52941 figure was a pre-f98.1/.2 measurement; f98.1 (pin reduce bridge callable contract) + f98.2 (keep boundary surfaces authoritative) already settled the convergence.

Actual current state of the three regression targets:
- fz_f98_range_reduce_scalar (bfh.1, reduce/3 over Range): ALL THREE PATHS PASS. Its defer.* flags are STALE and should be removed.
- fz_f98_range_reduce2 (bfh.2, reduce/2 over stepped Range): FAILS at transport.rs:338 — 'transport shape anchors disagree for connected position component'. The shared bridge reducer FunctionId(174) input0 is anchored to BOTH ShapeId(11) and ShapeId(14) within one connected union component (equalities cite transport.rs:1423/1887/1935). A shape-anchor conflict, NOT a return-ascent oscillation.
- fz_f98_range_map_converges (bfh.4, to_list Range+Map): FAILS at native lowering — 'native callable materialization for FunctionId(174)/0 matched multiple native boundaries' (e.g. [NativeCallableBoundaryId(8),(11)] for one published BoundaryId(21)). Same root cause one layer down: the shared bridge callable resolves to MULTIPLE boundaries.

REVISED LOCUS: the live defect is the shared bridge (FunctionId(174)) carrying MULTIPLE callable shapes/boundaries at ONE published transport position — the bfh.2 'multi-surface callable value resolved by native pick-first instead of producer identity' problem, surfacing as (a) conflicting transport ShapeId anchors and (b) multiple native boundaries. The fix belongs in transport callable-boundary identity / shape anchoring, NOT in the semantic return join. Next: determine whether ShapeId(11) vs (14) are layout-identical (interning/identity fragmentation — see [[feedback_shapeid_is_pure_layout]]) or genuinely divergent layouts (bridge needs per-shape boundary identity). The prior monotone-return fix is moot and was NOT implemented (good — it would not have touched these failures).

title: closure capture layout must not fragment on use-demand across specialized activations
